artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a topological space. A weakly first-countable structure (wfc-structure) on X is an assignment to every point x ∈ X of a sequence {B(n,x) : n ∈ ω} of subsets of X containing x, such that: (i) B(n+1,x) ⊆ B(n,x) for every n ∈ ω and every x ∈ X; and (ii) a subset U ⊆ X is open if and only if for every x ∈ U there exists n ∈ ω with B(n,x) ⊆ U. A space X is called weakly first-countable if it admits such a wfc-structure (also known as a "weakly basic" wfc-structure).

The Souslin number (also called the cellularity) c(X) of X is the supremum of cardinalities of families of pairwise disjoint non-empty open subsets of X; c(X) is countable means every such family is at most countable (i.e. X has the countable chain condition).

Question: Suppose X is a weakly first-countable topological space whose Souslin number is countable. Must |X| ≤ 2^{ω}?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is listed as a long-standing open problem of Arhangel'skii (pre-1980), modeled on the Hajnal–Juhász bound for first-countable ccc spaces. A 2023 work constructs ZFC examples of weakly first-countable compact spaces that are not first-countable, but these examples have cardinality ω₁ ≤ 2^ω and so do not violate the bound. No source found resolves the cellularity version of the question, and it continues to be cited as open.
